messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) water freezes at roughly **–2 °C**.  
This is slightly below the normal 0 °C freezing point at 1 atm because the melting/freezing temperature of water decreases as the external pressure falls. The exact value depends on the purity of the water and the precision of the phase‑diagram data, but –2 °C is the commonly cited figure for 10 kPa.
